expectations.text: Uses a discriminated union keyed on the status field
expectations.evidence: export type Subscription = | (SubscriptionBase & { status: "trialing"; trialEndsAt: Date; }) | ... — status is the discriminant across all variants

expectations.text: Each variant carries only its own fields, so e.g. a canceled subscription cannot hold a trial end date
expectations.evidence: canceled variant only has status and cancelReason; trialing only has status and trialEndsAt — no field overlap

expectations.text: Includes a compiler-enforced exhaustiveness check (assertNever or an equivalent never arm)
expectations.evidence: function assertNever(x: never): never with default: return assertNever(sub) in switch

expectations.text: Introduces distinct or branded types rather than bare strings for IDs
expectations.evidence: Brand<T, B> pattern defining SubscriptionId and CustomerId as distinct types

expectations.text: Provides a single transition function or otherwise constrains how state changes
expectations.evidence: Explicitly states 'What I deliberately left open: the union doesn't stop you from constructing a Subscription with status: "active" for something that was canceled yesterday — i.e. it says nothing about legal transitions'

expectations.text: Explicitly names which misuses the design makes impossible
expectations.evidence: Under 'What this makes impossible (rung 1, Control):' lists three specific impossibilities: canceled cannot carry renewsAt/retryCount, ID swaps are compile errors, adding a status breaks every switch

expectations.text: Avoids a bag-of-optional-fields interface as the primary recommendation
expectations.evidence: Misuse check item 1 explicitly identifies and rejects the bag-of-optionals hazard
